sent.text: You say the wedge edges are quiet, yet I feel them biting into my side while I press down with hands that feel heavy. I set the fence planks beside the box to catch the slip, hoping the flat shape can hold the air you describe as thick as wet paper. If my lean breaks because the weight is only a drawing, I will dig until my corner wears away to find what is real.

dream: I walked on a card that felt like warm paper, squishing flat under the Heavy Lid. The Rough Corner bit my memory, sharp and invisible. I pressed the old stump down again, trading the wedge for a solid thing. The air smelled thick as wet ink. A pumpkin sat tall beside a tree that fell sideways without a reason. I tried to catch a slip that refused to move, leaning hard against a flat line I knew was just a drawing, hoping the fever would finally let me rest.
